findings.title: Failure injection may trigger on the sign call instead of the final verify
findings.message: The fake `subprocess.run` raises on any call whose last argument is the output bundle path. A `codesign --sign` call typically ends with the bundle path too, so the failure may fire at signing instead of at the final verification. The test then passes without exercising cleanup after a failed final verification, which is what its name claims. Another test pins the verify call as `["codesign","--verify","--strict",str(output)]`, so the two can be told apart.
findings.suggestion: Match only the verify invocation, for example `if arguments[:3]==["codesign","--verify","--strict"]:raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(1,arguments)`. Also assert that the sign call happened before the failure.

findings.title: Temp archive inside the repo breaks the post-packaging clean-state check
findings.message: The temp file `.vellum-sdk-*` is created in `output.parent` before the final cleanliness re-check. If `output.parent` is inside the repository and not git-ignored, `git status --porcelain` reports it as untracked. `source_state(root)` then differs from the earlier `state`, so a public build fails with a misleading 'source changed during packaging' error. The same cause can make a private build pick up its own partially written temp archive, but only if the temp file lands under an allowed source directory.
findings.suggestion: Create the temp file in a directory outside the working tree (e.g. a `tempfile.mkdtemp` directory) and move it into place, which requires the same filesystem as `output`. Alternatively, reject output paths inside `root`, or compare the tracked-file state and ignore the temp path before the final check.

findings.title: Ambient GOROOT passes through the 'controlled' child environment
findings.message: GOROOT is forwarded from the ambient environment while the module forces GOTOOLCHAIN=local and the spec says ambient toolchain overrides are dropped. An inherited GOROOT can point the go command at a different, possibly untrusted, toolchain or standard library. That undermines the controlled build environment for verifying and executing archive code. PKG_CONFIG_PATH is forwarded in the same way and can influence cgo flags.
findings.suggestion: Do not forward GOROOT. Let the go binary found on PATH determine its own root. If an override is needed, validate it explicitly or make it opt-in. Consider the same for PKG_CONFIG_PATH.
